description: Start AI brief generation for one pillar of an owned brand and return the job ID. The pillar must belong to that brand. Up to five briefs (default five) are written per call; an optional primary_keyword steers the research and guidance adds a topic idea and a search intent. Each generated brief counts toward the organization's plan monthly brief allowance, and the run may also use its search research allowance; it takes no content allowance. Model usage is not separately metered, and a failed run does not consume brief allowance. A call that would exceed the brief allowance is refused with 429, and a generation already running for that brand is refused with 409 naming the job to poll. A 409 with Retry-After and no job id means another start is still being accepted for the organization; honor Retry-After, then retry the same key. A 503 before a job exists means the start could not be accepted; retry, and resend the same key to recover a job that key already names. There is no dry run. Saved briefs wait in review and are not approved by this operation: review and approve each one separately before creating an item from it. Requires a stable idempotency key. Poll GET /jobs/{job_id} with the returned job ID for progress and the outcome. On a lost response, resend the same key and body to get that one job back (Idempotency-Replayed: true); once it has ended, start again with a new key.

body.description:
Ask RoboWrite to write briefs for one pillar (request).

``brand_id`` and ``pillar_id`` are required and the pillar must belong to
that brand. ``num_briefs`` defaults to 5 and is capped at 5, the smaller of
the dashboard maximum and five briefs per call. ``primary_keyword`` is the
keyword the run researches; omit it to use the pillar's first keyword.

anyOf.description:
Accepted brief generation; poll ``GET /jobs/{job_id}`` for the outcome.

``status`` is ``running`` at dispatch, or ``queued`` when the job is
accepted but not yet assigned to a run.

status.description:
Status of a background job.

Terminal states: ``completed``, ``completed_with_errors``, ``failed``,
``cancelled``. Active (in-progress) states: ``queued``, ``running``.

``awaiting_review`` is a third class: not terminal (work may resume after a
human action) and not active (no automatic progress is being made). Pollers
should treat it as stop-and-review rather than keep waiting for a terminal
status. It is intentionally in neither ``is_terminal`` nor ``is_active``.
